name: biomimicry-boundary
note: No line is adopted. Science has not settled where 'learning from nature' stops. This file declares candidate axes, codes cases against them, and evaluates several candidate lines side by side. A change to any cell, axis or line must be logged in changelog.jsonl (tools/boundary.py log); an unlogged edit fails the corpus check.

values.PARTIAL: holds for part of the case, or only with help from outside the case
values.CONTESTED: the literature reads it both ways; both readings are in the basis

axes.living: the thing itself metabolises and maintains itself
axes.evolved: its form was shaped by selection on a lineage
axes.heredity: it copies its own specification to offspring
axes.self_organized: its structure arises from its own dynamics, with no template imposed from outside
axes.regenerable: the conditions that made it can make it again without the original (a copy exists in physics, chemistry, or a surviving record)

L2_SPECIES.reads_as: H0 §6's word: 'Each lost species is a lost source of science'

L3_EVOLVED_DESIGN.reads_as: copying anything selection designed, including what organisms build

L4_SELF_ORGANIZED.reads_as: copying any structure that builds itself (crystals, reaction fronts, landforms)

L5_NON_HUMAN.reads_as: copying anything humans did not design

L6_NO_COPY.reads_as: what H0 §6's argument needs: 'A species has no copy anywhere' -- the source can be lost with nothing left to regrow it

cases.name: termite mound
cases.basis: living: the soil structure does not metabolise, but it is read as the colony's extended physiology (Turner); evolved: the building behaviour is selected, the shape is set by local soil and wind (HLD_004: wind-driven, Turner & Soar 2008); heredity: the colony reproduces, the mound does not; regenerable: needs the species

cases.name: Roman concrete lime clasts
cases.basis: self_organized: the healing step (lime clasts dissolve and reprecipitate calcite in a crack) runs by itself after placement, the structure was placed by people; regenerable: the surviving structures held the mechanism for ~2,000 years and it was reproduced in 2023 (HLD_005)

cases.name: crystal growth (snowflake, quartz)
cases.basis: form set by lattice symmetry, temperature and supersaturation; the same conditions regrow it anywhere

cases.name: nacre (mollusc shell)
cases.basis: a material, not an organism, but secreted by a living mantle on an organic template; the organism side of the line Roman concrete sits on from the human side

cases.name: diatom frustule
cases.basis: single-celled eukaryote; silica wall patterned per species

cases.name: magnetotactic bacterium (magnetosome chain)
cases.basis: prokaryote; genetically controlled magnetite crystals -- an organism growing a crystal

cases.name: Physarum slime mould network
cases.basis: one multinucleate cell; network pruned by flow (Simulators search-substitution/)

cases.name: virus capsid
cases.basis: living: no metabolism of its own, read as alive or not depending on definition; heredity: copies only inside a host; capsid self-assembles from subunits

cases.name: Belousov-Zhabotinsky reaction waves
cases.basis: humans mix the reagents; the spiral waves organise themselves; any lab can remake it

cases.name: river delta / braided channel network
cases.basis: dissipative landform; the same flow and sediment regrow the pattern, though not the particular delta

cases.name: autocatalytic chemical set (origin-of-life candidate)
cases.category: interacting substances at the living edge
cases.basis: the exact place science has not settled: copies itself in part, selection on chemistry is argued both ways, and whether a lost set could regrow is unknown
